acceptance.refresh: the importer extracts from pinned Git objects, applies the two documented test-module removals with exact anchors, verifies every derived digest and only then copies; it refuses when a shim is missing, and two consecutive runs produced identical files
acceptance.rail: the new heartwood-canonical flake check builds the crate in its own workspace and lock file and runs the retained tests in release profile; all 7 pass, including the quorum, reference-protection and DID tests

fixes_during_import: the vendored manifest needed the upstream dependency features radicle-crypto `std` and `radicle-git-ref-format`, radicle-git-ref-format `serde`, nonempty `serialize`
upstream's `refname!` skips validation outside debug assertions, so the shim defines an always-validating macro; the release-profile check exposed this

serde_json `preserve_order` was briefly enabled for upstream's symbolic-reference tests, but it unifies globally and changed JSON map ordering for every workspace crate (a kiln-hosted migration test failed); it was removed and the symbolic test module is not run
excluded_upstream: The rest of the radicle crate is not imported: it depends on the sqlite crate, whose sqlite3-sys links the native sqlite3 library already linked by the workspace's rusqlite/libsqlite3-sys, and Cargo permits one links value per graph
trade_offs: The five shim files are Kiln-maintained and must track upstream module-path changes
Two fixture-dependent test modules are removed; upstream storage/identity integration is not exercised here, only the canonical algorithm and its retained unit tests
Upstream fixes after 71a91042 require a recorded refresh rather than a version bump
No Kiln crate consumes the module yet; the canonical source mode of #19 is the named consumer
